name: PostgreSQL
summary: A client/server relational database whose process architecture, multiversion concurrency control, and extension interfaces expose a broad and durable execution platform.

features.name: Process-oriented client/server sessions
features.description: PostgreSQL uses a client/server model with a server process managing database files and accepting connections. The server starts a separate process for each client connection in the documented architecture.
benefits: Separates client applications from database file ownership
Provides process boundaries for session work
costs: Network and process coordination add latency and operational complexity
The server becomes an independently managed availability boundary

features.name: MVCC snapshot-based transaction isolation
features.description: PostgreSQL uses multiversion concurrency control. Its documented isolation levels provide command- or transaction-scoped snapshots, and serializable transactions add dependency monitoring that can reject non-serializable executions.
benefits: Allows readers and writers to overlap without reducing every read to a blocking lock
Makes isolation guarantees explicit through transaction levels
Provides a path from snapshot behavior to serializable execution guarantees
costs: Old row versions and visibility tracking require maintenance work
Serializable and repeatable-read transactions may need retries
Isolation semantics require application knowledge of snapshots and anomalies

features.name: Database-resident extension contract
features.description: PostgreSQL is designed so that loaded extensions can function like built-in features. The documented extension surface includes independently developed extensions and even external replication solutions.
benefits: Allows domain-specific capabilities to live close to relational data and execution
Extends types, functions, operators, and operational behavior without forking the core
Supports an ecosystem beyond the base server distribution
costs: Extensions share the database's compatibility and operational boundary
Version, security, and upgrade coordination become ecosystem concerns
Extension behavior can widen the effective system surface substantially

features.name: Explicit transaction isolation spectrum
features.description: PostgreSQL exposes Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable behavior with distinct visibility and anomaly guarantees, while its Read Uncommitted mode behaves like Read Committed internally.
benefits: Lets applications select a consistency/performance point per transaction
Makes concurrency anomalies part of an explicit contract
Supports stronger invariants without requiring every workload to pay the strongest cost
costs: Applications must understand and handle serialization failures
Stronger isolation can increase monitoring overhead and retries
A single database exposes several semantics that complicate application reasoning

mathematical_views.question: How do client connections, server processes, and database operations evolve through a distributed session lifecycle?
assumptions: The documented process model abstracts away platform-specific process details
Database file ownership remains with server-side processes
Network failures and process crashes are modeled as transition events

mathematical_views.question: Which row versions are visible to a transaction or command under each isolation level?
assumptions: Transactions and row versions can be represented by a visibility predicate
The view abstracts physical tuple and vacuum implementation details
Serialization failures are modeled as rejected state transitions

mathematical_views.question: Which new data types, functions, and replication behaviors can be added while retaining the database's extension contract?
assumptions: An extension satisfies the documented loading and compatibility contract
The model concerns composability at the database interface, not arbitrary semantic equivalence
Extension interactions may introduce constraints not present in the core system

benefits: Strong client/server separation and familiar multi-client operation
costs: More deployment, process, and connection-management overhead than an embedded engine

benefits: High read concurrency with explicit visibility semantics
costs: Version cleanup, visibility bookkeeping, and retry behavior

benefits: A broad and reusable database platform boundary
costs: Larger compatibility, security, and upgrade surface

benefits: Configurable consistency guarantees for different workloads
costs: Application complexity and possible serialization retries
